activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Get up means leave your bed.
activities.explanation: Get up describes the physical action of leaving your bed.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: The natural phrase for eating the morning meal is do breakfast.
activities.explanation: We say have breakfast, not do breakfast.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Make the bed is a normal expression for arranging the sheets.
activities.explanation: Make the bed is the established collocation.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Wake up and get up always mean exactly the same thing.
activities.explanation: Wake up means stop sleeping; get up means leave the bed, so they can refer to different moments.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Take out the rubbish means carry it outside.
activities.explanation: Take out the rubbish is used when rubbish is removed from a home.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Do the laundry refers to washing clothes.
activities.explanation: Laundry means clothes and other items that need washing.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Have a break means continue working without resting.
activities.explanation: Have a break means stop for a short rest.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Someone who is running late is delayed.
activities.explanation: Run late means be behind the expected schedule.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Go shopping normally requires the preposition to before shopping.
activities.explanation: The normal expression is go shopping, without to before shopping.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Set an alarm means choose the time when it will ring.
activities.explanation: You set an alarm for the time you want it to sound.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Work from home describes doing your job at home.
activities.explanation: Work from home identifies the place where the work is done.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Make time for exercise means deliberately find time for it.
activities.explanation: Make time for something means reserve time for that activity.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Have a shower describes an activity, not possession of a shower.
activities.explanation: Have can describe activities such as having a shower or breakfast.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Tidy the room means make the room neat and organised.
activities.explanation: Tidy means organise a place and remove disorder.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: In everyday English, people normally say make the laundry.
activities.explanation: The standard collocation is do the laundry.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: A person can wake up at six and get up at half past six.
activities.explanation: The two expressions refer to stopping sleep and leaving the bed, which may happen at different times.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Meet a deadline means finish something by the required time.
activities.explanation: A deadline is the final permitted time for a task.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Take a nap means sleep for a short time during the day.
activities.explanation: A nap is a short period of sleep, usually during the day.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: The sentence I go in bed at ten uses the standard preposition.
activities.explanation: The standard phrase is go to bed, not go in bed.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Make up lost time means compensate for a delay.
activities.explanation: Make up lost time means work to recover time lost through a delay.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Go shopping and go to the shops have exactly the same grammatical pattern.
activities.explanation: Go shopping has no to before the activity, while go to the shops includes to before a place.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Take a break and have a break are both acceptable expressions.
activities.explanation: Both collocations are natural; have a break is especially common in British English.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Someone can be running late even if they have not arrived yet.
activities.explanation: Running late describes being behind schedule, whether or not the person has arrived.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: Do the cleaning and make the cleaning are equally standard collocations.
activities.explanation: Do the cleaning is the standard collocation; make the cleaning is not natural here.

activities.instructions: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
activities.prompt: In I have a shower, have describes an activity rather than ownership.
activities.explanation: Have is part of the activity expression have a shower.
